metadata.style: The Simpsons cartoon illustration, bold black outlines, flat bright color fills, minimal shading, small black eye pupils. Occupy Uranus — the Simpson family on an interplanetary space adventure, hauling cargo across the galaxy in a beaten-up spacecraft to colonize Uranus, because nobody at City Hall read the proposal before approving it. Deep space vistas, alien worlds, rickety spacecraft held together with duct tape and optimism. Duff Beer sponsorship decals on everything. Nuclear-powered engines that probably shouldn't have passed inspection. Cargo bays full of Springfield's finest exports. Every surface has a sight gag, every warning label is misspelled, every airlock has a donut stuck in it somewhere. Background details packed with visual jokes. Flat surfaces, smooth gradients, reads clearly at small sizes.

images.prompt: location establishing shot — a new Springfield building, generic but packed with background gags. Sky gradients are smooth, surfaces are flat, everything reads clearly at small sizes.. Atmosphere: Functional space station rendered in the Simpsons' clean flat style — like a Krusty Burger but in space. Industrial but not threatening.. Mood: Safe harbor — the space truck stop between Springfield and Uranus. Everything works mostly fine and the vending machines only occasionally eat your money.. Space station exterior in Simpsons cartoon style — boxy modular sections connected by corridors, painted in municipal beige and institutional green. The Hauler docked at a port with fuel lines attached. A sign reads 'SPRINGFIELD ORBITAL SUPPLY DEPOT — A DIVISION OF GLOBEX CORPORATION' with smaller text: 'EMPLOYEES MUST WASH HANDS BEFORE RETURNING TO SPACE.' Supply crates stacked on platforms, some labeled 'FRAGILE — CONTAINS DONUTS' and 'ISOTOPE FUEL RODS — DEFINITELY NOT STOLEN.' A vending machine visible through a window. Welding sparks from a maintenance worker in a yellow hardhat. The station has the feel of a highway rest stop that happens to be in orbit. Note: Fallback shop image — must be generic enough for any waypoint. The Simpsons' ability to make any location feel like Springfield through signage and mundane details makes even a space station feel like home.

action scene — something's going wrong, but in the show's characteristic 'this is fine' energy. Sky gradients are smooth, surfaces are flat, everything reads clearly at small sizes.. Atmosphere: The Simpsons danger palette — reds and oranges cranked up, the colors the show uses when something is about to explode or already has.. Palette shift: Add warning reds and emergency oranges. Simpsons yellow hull against dark asteroid grey for maximum contrast. Cartoon impact stars and motion lines.. Mood: The Simpsons brand of peril — genuinely dangerous but somehow also funny. Like Homer falling down Springfield Gorge. You wince AND you laugh.. The Hauler weaving through a chaotic asteroid field — rocks of various sizes tumbling past, some uncomfortably close. The ship banking hard, engine trail curving. One asteroid has scraped the hull, leaving a visible scratch next to an existing bumper sticker. A dashboard warning light visible through the cockpit window showing a generic 'DANGER' indicator (rendered in the show's simple UI style). One asteroid in the foreground has a funny detail — maybe a fossilized fish skeleton embedded in it, or it's shaped suspiciously like a donut. Motion lines on the asteroids. The fuzzy dice swinging wildly. A Duff beer can floating loose in the cockpit, visible through the window. Note: Generic danger event. Must convey immediate threat while maintaining the Simpsons' ability to find humor in crisis. The scratched bumper sticker and the loose Duff can are the right tone — real danger, cartoon stakes.

mystery — the X-Files crossover episode energy, strange lights and odd phenomena. Sky gradients are smooth, surfaces are flat, everything reads clearly at small sizes.. Atmosphere: Simpsons spooky palette — the purples and greens from Treehouse of Horror episodes. Mysterious but still cartoon-safe.. Mood: Simpsons mystery — could be aliens (Kang and Kodos energy), could be a spatial anomaly, could be nothing. The show's approach to the unknown: curious, slightly nervous, ultimately goofy.. A strange cosmic phenomenon rendered in Simpsons style — a glowing nebula with unusual swirling patterns in Treehouse of Horror greens and purples, an unknown signal source pulsing with light. The Hauler approaching cautiously, cockpit instruments lit up with question marks and exclamation points on the dashboard displays. The nebula has a vaguely face-like pattern if you squint (but it might be pareidolia). A small alien probe or satellite visible near the anomaly — it could be from Rigel VII (Kang and Kodos' homeworld) or it could be an old Earth satellite that got lost. The scene is mysterious but rendered in the show's clean, non-threatening visual language. Stars visible through the translucent nebula gas. Note: Contrasts with Event-01 — mysterious rather than dangerous. The Treehouse of Horror color palette and the possibly-Rigellian probe connect to the show's mythology without requiring knowledge of it.

solar storm — a spectacular cosmic energy event, beautiful and dangerous, the Simpsons doing disaster-spectacle at full scale. Sky gradients are smooth, surfaces are flat, everything reads clearly at small sizes.. Atmosphere: Solar storm palette — blazing oranges, electric yellows, white-hot plasma waves spreading through space. The show's warning-red palette pushed into gorgeous spectacular territory. Everything too bright and beautiful to be safe.. Mood: Natural disaster, Springfield style — like a Springfield weather emergency but happening to the entire inner solar neighborhood. Impressive and troubling in equal measure, and clearly visible from Shelbyville.. A massive solar storm in progress — great sheets and waves of solar plasma sweeping through space in bold flat Simpsons style, rendered as sweeping curves of orange, yellow, and white energy. The Hauler taking evasive action — engine burning hard, hull catching the energy wave's illumination, an emergency shield panel deployed (looking exactly like a Reynolds Wrap reflective blanket, because this ship improvises under pressure). The storm is beautiful in the show's bold visual language — the same colors as a Simpsons sunset but angrier and larger. Warning lights on the hull blinking urgently. A dashboard indicator visible through the cockpit window: 'SOLAR STORM: SEVERE. SHIELDS: OPTIMISTIC.' Stars barely visible through the energy wash. Note: Event variant three — the solar storm contrasts with Event-01's asteroid chaos with a different kind of threat (energy versus objects). The 'SHIELDS: OPTIMISTIC' reading captures the ship's engineering philosophy perfectly.

derelict discovery — an abandoned spacecraft drifting in deep space, mysterious and compelling, the Simpsons does X-Files meets roadside attraction. Sky gradients are smooth, surfaces are flat, everything reads clearly at small sizes.. Atmosphere: Mystery space palette — the Treehouse of Horror cool purples and greens. The derelict lit by its own dying systems, eerie but rendered in the show's clean, non-threatening visual language.. Mood: Springfield curiosity — the specific enthusiasm of people who should know better but are absolutely going to investigate that creepy abandoned spaceship. Homer's approach to mysterious objects: poke it and see what happens.. A derelict spacecraft drifting in space — large, clearly older, covered in the accumulated drift of years. A different design from the Hauler: bulkier, more formal, painted in institutional grey-green with faded lettering reading 'S.S. SPRINGFIELD II — PREVIOUS COLONIAL ATTEMPT.' The ship is dark but not dead — power conduits flickering, emergency running lights blinking on long-dead batteries. An escape pod bay is open and empty (pods have been used). A scan display near the Hauler reads: 'VESSEL: DERELICT. AGE: OLDER THAN THE PLAN. LIFE SIGNS: NONE. STRUCTURAL INTEGRITY: CLASSIFIED. DONUT RESIDUE: DETECTED.' The scene rendered in cool mysterious tones, the derelict both ominous and weirdly familiar. Note: Event variant four — contrasting with Event-02's natural mystery, this is a human mystery. 'Previous Colonial Attempt' and the donut residue scan are the breadcrumbs of Springfield's space program history, and suggest this is not the first time someone tried this.

couch gag title card — bold, colorful, the promise of a half-hour of cheerful catastrophe scaled up to interplanetary colonization. Sky gradients are smooth, surfaces are flat, everything reads clearly at small sizes.. Atmosphere: Bright Simpsons teal-blue — Uranus rendered in the show's clean, appealing color language. NOT realistic or threatening — it looks like the background of a particularly ambitious couch gag. The planet is beautiful the way Springfield sunsets are beautiful: simple, bold, and unexpectedly moving for a cartoon.. Mood: 'In the proud tradition of Springfield's nuclear power industry, we now present: space colonization.' Epic, goofy, warm, and absolutely confident that everything will work out despite overwhelming evidence to the contrary.. Sweeping view of Uranus from space — the planet rendered in clean Simpsons teal-blue with smooth atmospheric banding and simple geometric rings catching warm yellow-orange light. Beautiful, inviting, cartoonishly appealing. The Hauler ('The Canyonero') approaching from lower-left — a boxy, yellow-hulled spacecraft with a comically oversized rocket engine, Duff Beer logo on the cargo bay, fuzzy dice hanging in the cockpit window, and a bumper sticker reading 'MY OTHER SHIP IS ALSO POORLY MAINTAINED.' Warm orange engine glow trailing behind. A half-eaten donut floating in the ship's wake (escaped through an airlock someone left open). Stars as simple white dots against deep blue-black. Wispy cartoon clouds of colorful nebula in the background. The composition conveys both the ridiculous scale of the adventure and the cheerful incompetence of the mission. Note: Main menu screen — should feel like the opening shot of a Simpsons episode where you immediately know this is going to be a space episode and it's going to be great. The ship's bumper stickers and the floating donut tell the whole story before the game even starts.

mid-belt — deep in the asteroid field, surrounded. . Zone accents (belt): #BDBDBD, #757575, #9E9E9E; secondary #795548, #FF9800. mining rush — a dense asteroid cluster with full industrial operations at peak activity, the belt's industrial heart. Earth from a higher orbit, showing the nightside — the dark face lit by aurora borealis ribbons rendered in the show's Treehouse of Horror green-purple palette, sweeping across the polar regions in bold cartoon curves. solar prominence — the sun erupting with a massive energy arch, close enough to be spectacular and alarming. Sky gradients are smooth, surfaces are flat, everything reads clearly at small sizes.. Zone accents (inner): #D32F2F, #FF6B35, #FF9800; secondary #FF9800, #FFC107. Atmosphere: Solar maximum — blazing oranges, yellows, and white-hot energy. The inner system at its most dramatic. The Simpsons warm palette cranked to absolute maximum.. Mood: Overwhelming natural power — the kind of thing that makes Homer say 'Woah' in a small voice. Even Springfield's most oblivious resident would acknowledge that the sun doing THAT is worth pausing for.. The sun partially in frame — a blazing yellow-white disc at the image edge with a massive solar prominence arching away from the surface. The prominence rendered in the show's bold style — a great curving arch of orange-yellow plasma, simple and clean but enormous. The Hauler caught in the arch's reflected light, hull blazing orange-yellow, an improvised solar filter deployed over the cockpit window (a simple grey tinted screen, like car window tint, because this ship improvises). Radiation warning lights on the hull exterior blinking amber. The scale is overwhelming — the sun's edge and the prominence dwarf the ship completely. Stars washed out by the solar glare. Note: Inner system fourth variant — a solar prominence provides maximum dramatic spectacle while fitting the inner zone's heat palette. The improvised solar filter made from car window tint is the Simpsons' approach to radiation shielding.
